content: It is considered best practice and highly recommended to complete the Edit Summary field when making changes to a page. This is especially important when editing specific sections, as it helps both you and other contributors understand the nature of the changes made. This is particularly useful when reviewing the page's history. To ensure you do not forget to provide an edit summary, it is advisable to adjust your user preferences under the Edit section to enable the option Prompt me when entering a blank edit summary. When writing edit summaries, always fill in the summary field. This is regarded as an essential guideline. Even a brief summary is better than leaving it blank. Providing an edit summary becomes even more critical when deleting text, as failing to explain the deletion may lead others to suspect malicious intent. Additionally, if you mention one change but omit another, it can mislead readers who might find the omitted change more significant. To avoid this, you can add and misc. to cover any additional changes. Accurate edit summaries are valuable because they help others decide whether it is worth their time to review the changes. Well-written summaries often attract the attention of contributors with expertise in the relevant area. While detailed summaries may not always be necessary for minor changes, even a simple note like fixed spelling is appreciated. The edit summary box has a character limit of 200. If you attempt to paste more than 200 characters, only the first 200 will be displayed, and the rest will be discarded. For example, if you add 10 new characters to a summary that already contains 195 characters, only the first 5 new characters will be included, and the remaining 5 will be ignored. For small additions to an article, it is highly recommended to copy the full text of the addition into the summary field. This provides maximum information with minimal effort. You can use ft as an abbreviation for full text to indicate this. This approach allows readers to understand the extent of the edit without needing to check the page itself. Such edits also make it easier to review recent changes, page history, and user contributions efficiently, reducing server load. If the addition exceeds 200 characters and cannot fit entirely in the edit summary box, you should write a concise summary of the changes introduced. For example, if you add 400 characters, you can save time by copying the text into the summary field. The excess will be truncated, and the first 200 characters will usually suffice as a basic summary. However, note that only one line of text can be copied from the edit box into the summary box. Additional lines can be manually pasted at the end of the line. For edits involving bulleted lists, such as a see also section, it can be cumbersome to include the entire list in the summary box. One workaround is to place the list on a single line, separated by asterisks for the bullets, copy it into the summary box, and then format it properly in the main edit box. In addition to summarizing the change itself, the summary field can also include an explanation of the change. If the reason for an edit is unclear, it is more likely to be reverted, especially if text has been deleted. For longer explanations, use the Talk page and include see Talk in the edit summary. Once the page is saved, the summary cannot be edited, so it is important to avoid spelling errors. If there are significant omissions or errors in the summary, you can make a dummy edit to correct the summary. The edit summary appears in several places, including the page history (a list of changes to the page you edited), user contributions (a list of all your edits), the watchlist (a list of recent changes to watched pages for logged-in users), diff pages (showing the difference between two edits), recent changes (a list of all recent edits), Wikipedia IRC channels (a real-time list of all edits), related changes (a list of recent changes to pages linked to the page you edited), and the list of new pages (showing the edit summary of the page creation). Using the enhanced watchlist allows you to see all recent changes in watched pages, not just the last change in each page. Experienced users often use abbreviations in edit summaries to save time, such as rv for revert. While these abbreviations can be confusing for inexperienced users, they are generally acceptable for minor edits like formatting or grammar corrections. A list of commonly used abbreviations can be found in the Edit Summary Legend. The Wikimedia search function cannot search edit summaries, and they are not indexed by external search engines. When uploading an image, you can provide an upload summary. This serves multiple purposes, such as being part of the automatically created edit summary in the upload log, appearing as text in the image history entry, and serving as the edit summary for the creation of the image page. The upload summary can include a brief description of the image, internal or external links, template calls, and category specifications. The upload summary has a character limit of 250, and the last part may be truncated in the upload log. There is no preview function to check the code for links, template calls, or category tags, but you can edit the image page after uploading to correct errors or extend the text. When adding a new section to a discussion page using the + button, the section title is used as the edit summary. When editing an existing section, the section title is automatically inserted at the beginning of the edit summary, enclosed in /and / marks. Details of the edit should be added after this text. If you provide a long summary, you can delete the section title to stay within the 200-character limit. When viewing such an edit summary, the section name will appear in grey with a small link next to it, allowing users to view the section. If the section no longer exists, the link will redirect to the page. If you create a new section before or after an existing section by clicking a section edit link, delete the text between /and / marks to avoid confusion. It is also possible to manually include links to multiple sections using the /-/ syntax, which can be useful when editing several sections at once. When starting a new thread on a Talk page, the Post a comment feature can be used. Clicking the + sign next to the Edit link opens a box labeled Subject/headline. Text entered in the subject field becomes both the edit summary and a new heading, while text entered in the main edit box is inserted below this heading. In certain circumstances, an automatic summary is generated when an edit is saved without one. This is slightly different from the summary added when editing a section, as the latter can be modified by the user before saving. Automatic summaries are not a substitute for a proper edit summary and should not be relied upon. However, they can provide some context for edits made by inexperienced users and help identify vandalism. Text in edit summaries renders internal links, including piped links and interwiki links. Other wikitext coding is not interpreted. URLs are rendered as clickable links, showing the URL in parentheses. Copying wikitext into the edit summary box may be preferable to copying text from the preview, except when saving space is a priority.
